speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an infant presenting with recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing, particularly during specific activities. To begin our assessment, is this breathing difficulty more prominent when you are feeding, crying, or lying down?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia. The clinical presentation of inspiratory stridor and wheezing exacerbated by feeding, crying, and neck flexion, along with post-prandial vomiting, is classic for laryngomalacia. No further tests are required for this clinical diagnosis.
